title: The Smallest Missing Number in Each Range

concept.title: Sweep the right end; keep for every value the last place where it was seen, and descend to the first value last seen before l
body: The **mex** of a group of numbers is the smallest non-negative integer that is missing from it. For the range `2 3` of the list `1 0 2 0 3 1` the numbers are `0 2`, and the mex is 1. Each question asks for the mex of a range `l..r`. Looking at every value from 0 upward costs O(n) per question.

Answer the questions **offline**, sorted by their right end `r`. Sweep a position `pos` from left to right and keep, for every value `v`, `last[v]`: the last position `<= pos` where `v` occurred (or -1). A value `v` is present in the range `l..pos` exactly when `last[v] >= l`. So the mex of `l..pos` is the **smallest `v` with `last[v] < l`**. Store `last` in a segment tree over the values `0..n+1` that keeps the **minimum** in every node, and find that `v` by a descent: at each node go left if the minimum of the left child is `< l` (a missing value is there), otherwise go right.

Values larger than `n` can be ignored, because the mex of a range of at most `n` numbers is at most `n`. The leaves beyond `n + 1` keep the value -1, so the descent always finds a leaf. Each update and each question costs O(log n).

statement: A list of `n` non-negative integers is given. Answer `q` questions. Each question has two positions `l` and `r`: find the smallest non-negative integer that does not occur among the numbers at the positions `l` to `r` (counting from 1, both included). Print the answers on one line, in the order of the questions.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `q`: the length of the list and the number of questions.
The second line has the `n` numbers of the list.
Each of the next `q` lines has two numbers `l` and `r`.

examples.note: The whole list holds 0, 1, 2 and 3, so the missing one is 4. The range 2..3 holds 0 and 2: 1. The range 4..6 holds 0, 3 and 1: 2. The answers are 4 1 2.

hints: Process the questions sorted by r, moving a pointer over the list.
Keep for each value the last position where it occurred. A value is missing from l..r exactly when its last position before r is less than l.
Store these positions in a segment tree with the minimum in every node, and descend to the leftmost value whose last position is less than l.

explanation: The questions are answered offline in the order of their right end. A segment tree over the values keeps the last position of each value (minimum in every node); the mex of l..r is found by descending to the leftmost value whose last position is less than l.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + q) log n), space O(n + q).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, q = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
qs = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

size = 1
while size < n + 2:
    size *= 2
mn = [-1] * (2 * size)
by_r = [[] for _ in range(n)]
for j in range(q):
    by_r[qs[j][1] - 1].append(j)
ans = [0] * q
for pos in range(n):
    v = a[pos]
    if v <= n:
        i = v + size
        mn[i] = pos
        i >>= 1
        while i:
            left = mn[2 * i]
            right = mn[2 * i + 1]
            mn[i] = left if left < right else right
            i >>= 1
    for j in by_r[pos]:
        l = qs[j][0] - 1
        node = 1
        while node < size:
            if mn[2 * node] < l:
                node = 2 * node
            else:
                node = 2 * node + 1
        ans[j] = node - size
print(*ans)
